t: A company purchases a fleet of 20 cars for its sales executives and claims deficiency in the extended warranty service. For the purpose of Section 2(7) the company is:
o: A consumer, because companies are juristic persons
A consumer only for the first car
A consumer, since services were availed
Not a consumer, as the cars were obtained for a commercial purpose
e: Goods or services obtained for a commercial purpose fall outside Section 2(7); the livelihood-by-self-employment exception does not apply to a company's business fleet.

t: Which element is NOT required for a person to be a 'consumer' under Section 2(7)?
o: Consideration paid, promised or partly paid
Use for resale or commercial purpose
Use with approval, in the case of a beneficiary
e: Use for resale or commercial purpose is an exclusion, not an ingredient; the definition requires consideration (paid, promised or deferred) for goods bought or services hired, and covers approved users and beneficiaries.

t: Which procedural facilities were introduced by the 2019 Act to reduce inconvenience to consumers?
o: Compulsory legal representation and oral evidence
Electronic filing of complaints and hearing/examination of parties through video-conferencing
Filing only at the seller's registered office
e: The 2019 Act contains enabling provisions for e-filing of complaints and for hearing or examining parties through video-conferencing, along with filing at the consumer's place of residence or work.

t: In a product liability action under the 2019 Act, which three persons may be made liable for a claim for compensation?
o: Product manufacturer, product service provider and product seller
e: The product liability chapter brings within its scope the product manufacturer, product service provider and product seller for claims arising from a defective product or deficient service.

t: Compared with a product seller or service provider, the liability of a product manufacturer under the 2019 Act is:
o: Lower, since manufacturers are regulated by BIS
Higher, as the manufacturer is liable even without negligence or fraud in an express warranty
Nil if the product carries an ISI mark
e: The Act imposes stricter liability on manufacturers, who cannot escape by proving absence of negligence or fraud in making an express warranty, while sellers have defences such as misuse or alteration.

t: A manufacturer convicted for a subsequent misleading advertisement offence may be fined up to ₹50 lakh and imprisoned for up to:
e: For a subsequent offence the fine may extend to ₹50 lakh and imprisonment up to five years, against ₹10 lakh and two years for the first offence.

t: An endorser of a misleading advertisement is found guilty for the first time. Under the 2019 Act the CCPA may bar him from endorsing that product for a period up to:
e: The first prohibition is up to one year; for every subsequent offence the prohibition may extend to three years.

t: A consumer paid ₹1.5 crore for a flat and complains of deficiency. The complaint lies before the:
e: Consideration above ₹50 lakh but not exceeding ₹2 crore falls within the State Commission's original jurisdiction under Section 47(1)(a)(i).

t: A revision petition before the State Commission under Section 47(1)(b) must be filed within:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Regulation 14(1)(i) of the Consumer Protection (Consumer Commission Procedure) Regulations, 2020 prescribes 90 days for revision petitions before the State Commission and the NCDRC.

t: An appeal against the District Commission's order passed under Section 72 for non-compliance of its order lies to the State Commission under Section 73 within:
e: Section 73(1)(a) provides a 30-day period, with power to condone delay, for appeals against non-compliance orders, unlike the 45 days for ordinary appeals under Section 41.

t: The 30-day period for filing a review petition before the District Commission is traceable to:
o: Section 40 read with Regulation 14(1)(iii) of the Consumer Commission Procedure Regulations, 2020
e: Section 40 confers the power of review on the District Commission and Regulation 14(1)(iii) of the 2020 Regulations fixes 30 days.

t: An insurer receives notice of a consumer complaint on 1 July. If it obtains the full extension, the last date for filing its written version is:
e: The reply is due within 30 days (31 July), extendable by a further 15 days under Sections 38(2)(a)/38(3)(a), giving 15 August as the outer limit.

t: A second appeal to the NCDRC against a State Commission order passed in its appellate jurisdiction is permitted under Section 51(2) only if:
o: The complainant is a senior citizen
It involves a substantial question of law
e: Section 51(2) permits a second appeal to the NCDRC only where the case involves a substantial question of law, within 30 days.

t: An appeal from the NCDRC's order in a consumer complaint lies to the Supreme Court within:
e: Under Section 51 (and Section 73(1)(c) for non-compliance orders) an appeal to the Supreme Court lies within 30 days, with power to condone delay.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Requirements of policy
t: Which of the following is NOT a component of the compulsory cover in Section 147(1)(b)(i)?
o: Death of any person caused by use of the vehicle in a public place
Bodily injury to the owner of goods carried in the vehicle
Damage to property of a third party
Damage to the insured vehicle itself
e: Section 147(1)(b)(i) covers third-party death, bodily injury (including owner of goods or representative) and third-party property damage; own damage is not part of the statutory cover.

t: Three persons travel free of charge in a goods carriage along with the consignment. After the 2019 amendment, the insurer's statutory liability for their injuries under Section 147(1)(b)(ii) is:
o: Limited to the Compensation Act amount
Full, as passengers of a transport vehicle
Nil, since gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle are excluded
e: The amended clause excludes gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle from the mandatory passenger cover; such liability can only be covered by a separate extension.

t: The Explanation to Section 147(1) was inserted 'for the removal of doubts' to clarify that:
o: Only accidents on highways are covered
The victim need not be in a public place if the act or omission leading to the accident occurred in a public place
Passengers of goods vehicles are excluded
e: The Explanation deems death, injury or property damage to arise out of use in a public place even if the victim or property was not in a public place, provided the causative act occurred in a public place.

t: The 2019 amendment to Section 166 reintroduced a limitation period for filing a claim application before the Claims Tribunal of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 166(3) as inserted in 2019 provides that no application for compensation shall be entertained unless made within six months of the occurrence of the accident.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Limits of liability
t: The un-amended Section 147(2)(b) fixed the compulsory limit for third-party property damage at ₹6,000. Under the India Motor Tariff, insurers nevertheless provide TPPD cover of ₹7.5 lakh, with the option to restrict to ₹6,000 against a premium discount. An insured who chose the ₹7.5 lakh cover damages property worth ₹4 lakh. The insurer pays:
e: Where the insured has not opted for the statutory restriction, the policy covers TPPD up to ₹7.5 lakh, so the actual damage of ₹4 lakh is payable.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Certificate of insurance
t: Under Section 147(3), the certificate of insurance must contain:
o: The prescribed particulars of any condition subject to which the policy is issued and other prescribed matters
The claim history of the insured
e: The certificate must be in the prescribed form, containing particulars of any condition subject to which the policy is issued and any other prescribed matters; different forms may be prescribed for different cases.

t: The seven-day notification requirement in Section 147 is triggered when:
o: A policy is cancelled for non-payment
A cover note is not followed by a policy within the prescribed/specified time
e: When a cover note issued under Chapter XI is not followed by a policy within the specified time, the insurer must, within seven days of expiry of the cover note's validity, notify the registering authority.

t: Under the amended Section 147, the Compensation Act referred to in the employee proviso is:
e: The Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 was renamed the Employees' Compensation Act in 2010, and the amended Section 147 refers to it by that name.

t: The phrase 'notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force' in Section 147(5)/(6) means that the insurer's obligation to indemnify the persons specified in the policy:
o: Overrides contrary provisions of other laws
Is limited to the Compensation Act amounts
Is subject to the Insurance Act only
e: The non-obstante clause gives Section 147's indemnity obligation overriding effect over any other law in force.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Requirements of policy
t: Which statement about Section 147 is correct?
o: The amended version dispenses with the certificate of insurance
Only the un-amended version requires an authorised insurer
Both the old and the amended sub-section (1)(a) require issue by an authorised insurer
The amended version requires issue by a public-sector insurer
e: Both versions retain clause (1)(a) requiring an authorised insurer and sub-section (3) requiring a certificate of insurance.

t: Which provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, which allowed compensation on a structured formula under the Second Schedule, was omitted by the 2019 amendment?
e: Section 163A (structured formula based on age and income, with a ₹40,000 income ceiling) was omitted along with Sections 140–144; Section 164 now provides fixed no-fault compensation.

t: A victim of a hit-and-run accident suffers grievous hurt in March 2024. Under the 2022 Scheme the compensation payable is:
e: The Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme, 2022 (effective 1 April 2022) provides ₹50,000 for grievous hurt and ₹2 lakh for death.

t: Under Section 173, the period for filing an appeal against an award of the Claims Tribunal before the High Court is:
e: Section 173 allows 90 days from the date of the award, with power to condone delay for sufficient cause, subject to the deposit of ₹25,000 or 50% of the award, whichever is less.

t: Although Section 30 of the Indian Contract Act makes wagering agreements void, an insurance contract is enforceable because:
o: The premium is paid in advance under Section 64VB
The insured has an insurable interest in the subject matter
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Insurable interest distinguishes insurance from a wager: the insured stands to lose on the happening of the event, so the contract is one of indemnity, not a bet.

t: Under the amended Section 159 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the police officer must forward the Detailed Accident Report to the Claims Tribunal and the insurer within:
e: The 2019 amendment requires the police to prepare and forward the accident information/Detailed Accident Report within three months, which can be treated as the claim application under Section 166(4).

t: Under Section 145 of the Motor Vehicles Act (as amended), 'third party' includes:
o: The Government, and the driver and other employees of a transport vehicle
e: The amended definition of 'third party' in Section 145 includes the Government, the driver and other employees of a transport vehicle, widening the class of persons protected.

t: A branch issues a shop policy on 1 May on the strength of an unconfirmed promise that the customer will pay next week. This violates:
e: Section 64VB prohibits assumption of risk before receipt of premium; no cover can commence on a mere promise to pay.

t: Under Section 64UM, a person may act as a surveyor and loss assessor only if he:
o: Is an employee of the insurer
Holds a valid licence/registration granted by IRDAI
e: Section 64UM read with the IRDAI (Insurance Surveyors and Loss Assessors) Regulations, 2015 requires a surveyor to hold a valid licence/certificate of registration from the Authority.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required under Section 6 of the Insurance Act, 1938 to carry on general insurance business is:
e: Section 6 requires ₹100 crore paid-up equity capital for life or general insurance (including health) and ₹200 crore for a reinsurer.

t: The current sectoral cap for foreign direct investment in an Indian insurance company, after the Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2021, is:
e: The 2021 amendment raised the FDI limit from 49% to 74% under the automatic route, subject to safeguards.

t: A premium cheque received on 10 June is dishonoured on 14 June. A claim occurs on 12 June. The insurer's position is:
o: Claim payable, as the loss occurred before dishonour
Claim not payable; the policy is void ab initio as no premium was received under Section 64VB
Claim payable if the insured pays premium in cash now
e: When a premium cheque bounces, premium is deemed never received; under Section 64VB the risk never attached and the policy is void from inception.

t: An Insurance Ombudsman can entertain a complaint where the value of the claim, including expenses, does not exceed:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The limit was raised to ₹50 lakh by the amended Insurance Ombudsman Rules.

t: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India is headquartered at:
e: IRDAI's head office is in Hyderabad; the 'of India' was added to its name by the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act, 2015.

t: The IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024 came into force on:
e: The consolidated 2024 regulations, which replaced eight earlier regulations including the PPHI Regulations 2017, took effect from 1 April 2024.

t: An insurer receives the surveyor's final report on a marine cargo claim on 1 August. Under the IRDAI 2024 framework the insurer must decide the claim within:
o: 7 days of receipt of the report
15 days of receipt of the report
30 days of receipt of the report
45 days of receipt of the report
e: The 2024 regulations/master circular require the insurer to settle or reject the claim within 7 days of receipt of the survey report (earlier 30 days under the 2017 regulations).

t: The Insurance Ombudsman must pass its award within what period of receipt of all requirements from the complainant?
e: The Ombudsman Rules require the award to be made within three months of receipt of all requirements from the complainant; proceedings are free of charge.

t: Under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 the insurer's maximum liability for relief arising from a single accident is:
e: The PLI Rules cap the insurer's liability at ₹5 crore per accident and ₹15 crore in aggregate for the policy year; relief beyond that comes from the Environmental Relief Fund.

t: Under the Schedule to the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 the relief for death of a person is:
e: The Schedule provides ₹25,000 for fatal accidents (in addition to reimbursement of medical expenses up to ₹12,500), with lower amounts for disability and up to ₹6,000 for property damage.

t: For calculating compensation under the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 the monthly wages are currently capped by Central Government notification at:
e: The wage ceiling under Section 4 was raised from ₹8,000 to ₹15,000 with effect from 3 January 2020.

t: A workman dies after an accident at work. Under the Employees' Compensation Act the employer must also pay funeral expenses of:
e: Section 4(4) requires the employer to deposit ₹5,000 towards funeral expenses with the Commissioner, in addition to the death compensation.

t: The IRDAI portal through which a policyholder can escalate an unresolved grievance against an insurer is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bima Bharosa (formerly IGMS) is the grievance portal; Bima Sugam is the marketplace, Bima Vahak the women-led distribution channel and Bima Vistaar the combined rural product.

t: Under Section 10 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 an agreement becomes a contract if it is made:
o: By free consent of competent parties, for lawful consideration and lawful object
e: Section 10 lists free consent, competency of parties, lawful consideration and lawful object; writing or registration is needed only where specifically required by law.

t: Match the forum with its limitation: (i) Insurance Ombudsman, (ii) consumer complaint, (iii) MACT claim, (iv) civil suit on policy. The correct periods are:
e: Ombudsman complaint within 1 year of rejection; consumer complaint within 2 years (Section 69 CPA); MACT claim within 6 months (Section 166(3) MV Act); civil suit within 3 years (Limitation Act, Article 44).

t: Under Section 7 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 an arbitration agreement must be:
e: Section 7 requires the arbitration agreement to be in writing, which may be a clause in the contract (such as a policy condition) or a separate agreement.

t: A branch notices that a customer buys and cancels several policies within the free-look period, each time seeking refund to a different bank account. The appropriate action is to:
o: Refund in cash to close the matter
Escalate for filing a Suspicious Transaction Report with FIU-IND through the Principal Compliance Officer
Ignore, as free-look cancellation is a right
e: Unusual patterns suggesting layering of funds must be reported as a Suspicious Transaction Report; under the PML Rules an STR is filed within 7 working days of the transaction being flagged as suspicious.

t: An RTI applicant aggrieved by the PIO's reply may file a first appeal with the officer senior in rank to the PIO within:
e: Section 19 provides 30 days for the first appeal to the designated First Appellate Authority; a second appeal lies to the Central Information Commission within 90 days.
